title: Finite coefficient comparison respects compact-support composition
statement:
Fix the finite-field and coefficient datum [def-weil-finite-field-fiber, def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]: $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$, $\ell\ne\operatorname{char}k$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$ and uniformizer $\varpi_E$, and $A_r=\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^r$ for $r\ge1$. Let $X\xrightarrow fY\xrightarrow gZ$ be separated finite-type morphisms of separated finite-type $k$-schemes [def-weil-finite-type-morphism, def-weil-proper-morphism]. Let $m\ge n\ge1$, $A=A_m$, $B=A_n$, and $Q_T=-\otimes_A^LB$ on the small etale sites, or on the finite constructible pro-etale realizations [def-weil-pbc-etale-site, def-weil-pbc-proetale-site, lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings]. Write $F_{h,r}=Rh_{!,r}$ for compact support [def-compact-support-direct-image-detailed, def-amb-etale-compact-support], $\alpha_{g,f,r}:F_{g,r}F_{f,r}\xrightarrow{\sim}F_{gf,r}$ for its canonical composition isomorphism [thm-sf-comp-composition, lem-amb-etale-compact-comparisons], and $q_{h,M}:Q_{\mathrm{target}(h)}F_{h,m}M\xrightarrow{\sim}F_{h,n}Q_{\mathrm{source}(h)}M$ for the canonical coefficient comparison [lem-fix-compact-support-coefficient-change]. For every $K\in D^b_{ctf}(X_{\mathrm{et}},A)$, or its finite constructible pro-etale realization, where this means a bounded constructible complex of $A$-module sheaves on $X$ with finite Tor amplitude (there exist integers $a\le b$ such that tensoring $K$ with any degree-zero $A$-module sheaf has cohomology only in $[a,b]$) [lem-sf-flat-model, def-weil-pbc-constructible-complexes, def-weil-finite-torsion-constructibility, def-weil-finite-tor-amplitude], the following equality holds:
$$
q_{gf,K}\circ Q_Z(\alpha_{g,f,m,K})
=\alpha_{g,f,n,Q_XK}\circ F_{g,n}(q_{f,K})\circ q_{g,F_{f,m}K}.
$$
Both sides are morphisms $Q_ZF_{g,m}F_{f,m}K\to F_{gf,n}Q_XK$. The comparisons on the pro-etale realization are the canonical ones for compactifications, with the site identifications of [lem-sf-class-compact-support-comparison].

source.place: Tag 0F7J (lemma-shriek-composition), construction of the composition comparison, together with Tag 0GL6 (remark-Rf-lower-shriek-change-of-rings); the displayed naturality square is an agent-explicit consequence of those constructions, not a verbatim assertion of either tag.

proof.text:
We first check the domains, independently of exceptional adjoints. A finite-type scheme over k is Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian], since a field is Noetherian, and is quasi-separated by [lem-weil-pbc-locally-noetherian-quasi-separated]. All morphisms between the finite-type schemes used here are qcqs by [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence]. Choose a compactification (i:Y→Ybar,s:Ybar→Z) of g by [thm-nagata-compactification]. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-compatible-compactification-triangle] to obtain a:X→Xbar and p:Xbar→Ybar compactifying if, V=Xbar×_{Ybar}Y with b:V→Xbar open and r:V→Y proper, and j:X→V open, with bj=a and rj=f. Thus (j,r), (i,s), (a,sp) compactify f,g,gf. These ambient schemes are finite type over k: proper maps are finite type, and each ambient scheme is proper over a finite-type k-scheme. The open subscheme V is Noetherian and quasi-compact, and its immersion is quasi-compact as stipulated by the triangle lemma.

In a compactification h=t v, extension by zero takes finite-Tor constructible input to finite-Tor constructible input by [lem-trf-open-ctf]. The ambient scheme has a finite dimension bound by [lem-kun-dimension-finite-type] (choose bound 0 if empty). Apply [cor-sf-direct-image-ctf-proetale] to the proper map t. It follows that F_{h,m}K is finite-Tor constructible. In particular F_{f,m}K is an allowed argument of q_g; this check does not use any exceptional or Verdier coefficient theorem.

source.place: Tag 0F7J (lemma-shriek-composition), first compactification diagram; domain checks for its finite-field specialization

proof.text: Reduction has the required bounded domain even though A→B need not be flat. By [lem-sf-flat-model] and [lem-sf-reduction-flat-model], a bounded flat representative P of K gives QK=P⊗_A B, bounded and flat over B in the same interval. On the pro-etale site, [lem-pur-finite-tensor-constructible-cohomology] applied to K and the constant finite A-module B gives constructible underlying A-cohomology. Since A→B is surjective, a trivialization of such an A-module sheaf is B-linear: the B-action is the action of any A-lift, independent of the lift because the kernel acts as zero. Thus this is constructibility over B as well. The tensor comparison of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback] identifies this with ν_T^*(QK) for an etale input. Apply [lem-sf-bounded-below-ctf-reflection] to conclude that this bounded etale reduction is finite-Tor constructible. For an etale compact-support output C, its bounded-below witness and its pro-etale realization are supplied by [lem-sf-class-compact-support-comparison]. Step 1 proves that realization finite-Tor constructible; the same reflection lemma therefore applies to C. Conversely [lem-sf-proetale-constructible-origin] supplies bounded constructible etale representatives of pro-etale inputs, and [lem-sf-comparison-tor-amplitude] identifies their Tor intervals. We may now work in the ordinary etale derived categories; the ambient maps below do not require finite-Tor bounds, which are used for the displayed q maps and final site comparison.

source.place: Tag 0GL6 (remark-Rf-lower-shriek-change-of-rings); bounded finite-Tor specialization and site-domain checks

proof.text:
Fix the normalization of the coefficient maps. Write L_{u,D}=u_D^{-1}, R_{u,D}=Ru_{*,D}, and I_{v,D}=v_{!,D} for D=A,B. The derived scalar extension Q is the ringed-topos pullback for the identity topos with coefficient map A→B [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings, lem-weil-pbc-ringed-projection-mate-exact]. For any u let
$$\lambda_u:L_{u,B}Q_T\xrightarrow{\sim}Q_WL_{u,A},\qquad u:W\to T.$$
On K-flat representatives it is the coefficient-linear identification u^{-1}(x⊗b)↦u^{-1}x⊗b, using [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback]. Its mate is the B-linear map
$$\chi_{u,M}:Q_TR_{u,A}M\to R_{u,B}Q_WM,$$
whose transpose is Q_W(ε_{u,A,M}) λ_{u,R_{u,A}M}. This is precisely the normalization in [lem-coef-finite-direct-image], not just an underlying-A projection map.

For an open v:W→T define β_v:Q_TI_{v,A}→I_{v,B}Q_W by the identity between the right adjoints of these two composite left adjoints: restriction of scalars and open restriction commute on the underlying sheaf. The inverse δ_v has transpose under I_{v,B}⊣L_{v,B}
$$Q_WM\xrightarrow{Q_W\eta_{v,A,M}}Q_WL_{v,A}I_{v,A}M\xrightarrow{\lambda_v^{-1}}L_{v,B}Q_TI_{v,A}M.$$
The open adjunction and its exact derived descent are supplied by [lem-amb-etale-adjoint-locality]. Transposing the inverse identity and applying the triangle identities gives an inverse, so β_v is an isomorphism. On tensor representatives its underlying map is the open tensor comparison: both restrict to x⊗b↦x⊗b on the open and are zero off it. For a compactification h=t v, put
$$q_h^{(v,t)}=R_{t,B}(\beta_v)\circ\chi_t I_{v,A}.$$
This is the canonical tensor coefficient comparison of [lem-fix-compact-support-coefficient-change]: the proper factor is the counit-defined projection arrow, and the open factor is extension-by-zero tensor comparison, exactly the two factors of [def-exchange-projection]. This identification is made in D(B) by the displayed adjunction transposes. Equality of underlying A-arrows alone is not used.

source.place: Tag 0GL6 and Tag 0GL5 (lemma-projection-formula-Rf-lower-shriek), proper/open construction of the coefficient map; agent-explicit B-linear normalization

proof.text:
The elementary inverse-image/coefficient squares λ commute with composition: on K-flat representatives both paths identify (vu)^{-1}(x⊗b) with u^{-1}v^{-1}x⊗b. Pasting along adjunctions in [lem-weil-pbc-mate-pasting](2) therefore gives
$$\chi_{vu}=R_{v,B}(\chi_u)\circ\chi_vR_{u,A}$$
after the direct-image compositors. On the finite-Tor objects this is also the explicit composition assertion of [lem-coef-finite-direct-image]. For two opens v,w, transposing β_{wv} and (I_{w,B}β_v)(β_w I_{v,A}) gives the same identity of the three right-adjoint factors, so they agree. The canonical open compositor is [lem-cbc-extension-zero-composition]. These are equations of B-linear transformations and remain valid with arbitrary extra functors whiskered on either side.

source.place: Tag 0F7J, second equality of its four-line calculation; canonical direct-image and open-extension compositors

proof.text:
We need the compatibility for the middle proper/open interchange, not merely for a pair of proper maps. For the cartesian square (b:V→Xbar,r:V→Y,i:Y→Ybar,p:Xbar→Ybar), let E_D:L_{i,D}R_{p,D}→R_{r,D}L_{b,D} be the ordinary open-restriction exchange. It is the adjunction mate of the inverse-image square by [def-kun-unbounded-exchange]. The two pastings of this inverse-image square with the four λ squares agree: they apply the same inverse images to x and leave its coefficient b unchanged. Apply both pasting laws in [lem-weil-pbc-mate-pasting] to this equality. Their mates give the typed identity, for N on Xbar,
$$\chi_{r,L_{b,A}N}\,Q_Y(E_{A,N})\,\lambda_{i,R_{p,A}N}
=R_{r,B}(\lambda_{b,N})\,E_{B,Q_{Xbar}N}\,L_{i,B}(\chi_{p,N}).\tag{1}$$
Both sides go from L_{i,B}Q_{Ybar}R_{p,A}N to R_{r,B}Q_VL_{b,A}N. This is formal mate pasting, and requires no assertion that an arbitrary coefficient change is a geometric base change.

source.place: Tags 0F7B (lemma-shriek-proper-and-open) and 0F7J; agent expansion of inverse-image mate naturality under coefficient change

proof.text:
Write γ_D:I_{i,D}R_{r,D}→R_{p,D}I_{b,D} for the normalized proper/open interchange. By [lem-amb-unbounded-proper-open-interchange], it is the I_{i,D}⊣L_{i,D} transpose of t_D^{-1}, where
$$t_D=R_{r,D}(\eta_{b,D}^{-1})\,E_DI_{b,D}:L_{i,D}R_{p,D}I_{b,D}\xrightarrow{\sim}R_{r,D}.$$
In particular t_D L_{i,D}(γ_D)=1, with the canonical open unit inserted. Use (1) with N=I_{b,A}M. The formula for δ_b in step 3 gives the precise unit identity
$$Q_V(\eta_{b,A,M}^{-1})\,\lambda_{b,I_{b,A}M}
=\eta_{b,B,Q_VM}^{-1}\,L_{b,B}(\beta_{b,M}).$$
Postcompose (1) at N=I_{b,A}M with R_{r,B}Q_V(η_{b,A,M}^{-1}). Naturality of χ_r changes its left side to χ_{r,M} Q_Y(t_{A,M}) λ_{i,R_{p,A}I_{b,A}M}. On its right side substitute the displayed unit identity, and then use naturality of E_B at β_{b,M}. This gives the fully typed cancellation identity
$$t_{B,Q_VM}\,L_{i,B}\bigl(R_{p,B}(\beta_{b,M})\,\chi_{p,I_{b,A}M}\bigr)
=\chi_{r,M}\,Q_Y(t_{A,M})\,\lambda_{i,R_{p,A}I_{b,A}M}.$$
Both sides go from L_{i,B}Q_{Ybar}R_{p,A}I_{b,A}M to R_{r,B}Q_VM. For i, step 3 likewise gives
$$L_{i,B}(\beta_{i,N})\,\lambda_{i,I_{i,A}N}^{-1}\,Q_Y(\eta_{i,A,N})
=\eta_{i,B,Q_YN}.$$
Using these two identities and t_A L_{i,A}(γ_A)η_{i,A}R_{r,A}=1 gives
$$R_{p,B}(\beta_b)\,\chi_p I_{b,A}\,Q_{Ybar}(\gamma_A)
=(\gamma_BQ_V)\,I_{i,B}(\chi_r)\,\beta_iR_{r,A}.\tag{2}$$
To check that no isomorphism cancellation is hidden, transpose both sides under I_{i,B}⊣L_{i,B}, identifying their source with I_{i,B}Q_YR_{r,A} by β_i. Postcompose both transposes with t_B. On the left, (1) and t_A L_iγ_A=1 reduce this composite to χ_r; on the right, t_B L_iγ_B=1 gives χ_r directly. Since t_B is an isomorphism and the adjunction is a bijection, the two original arrows are equal. This proves (2) in D(Ybar_et,B).

source.place: Tag 0F7B, Cartesian open-square normalization of lemma-shriek-proper-and-open; Tag 0F7J, middle interchange

proof.text: Apply [lem-sf-proper-open-coefficient-refinement] to a proper refinement u:T_1→T_2 with uj_1=j_2. The ambient schemes are Noetherian by step 1. The input is bounded below, and its reduction is bounded below by step 2. The χ and β of step 3 have exactly the adjunction normalizations in that lemma, as does the refinement arrow of [def-weil-pbc-proper-open-comparison]. Its equation therefore makes the coefficient square for this arrow commute, without assuming that the refinement square is cartesian. A compact-support refinement comparison is proper composition followed by this arrow or its inverse. Step 4 gives the proper-composition coefficient square; paste the two squares, and invert them when necessary. Thus q_h^c commutes with each refinement. The cocycle and common-refinement assertion of [lem-amb-etale-compact-comparisons] extends this to the canonical comparison between any two compactifications. This is the required change-of-model assertion.

source.place: Tag 0F7I (lemma-shriek-well-defined), refinement comparison; Tag 0F7J, independence of compactifications
Tag 0F7J (lemma-shriek-composition), complete four-line proper/open computation, oriented Rg_!Rf_!→R(gf)_!

proof.text: Conjugate the equality in step 8 by the canonical comparisons from its three compactifications to the chosen compactifications for f,g,gf. Step 7 moves each q through these comparisons. The composition comparison commutes with these same comparisons by [lem-amb-etale-compact-comparisons]. Naturality moves the input comparison for f through the functor for g. Adjacent inverse comparisons cancel. The result is exactly the equation in the statement on the small etale sites, with both sides from Q_ZF_{g,m}F_{f,m}K to F_{gf,n}Q_XK.

source.place: Tag 0F7J, common-refinement independence and the canonical comparison of the three compactifications

proof.text: Finally verify that this is the asserted equation for the finite constructible pro-etale realization as well. The compactification functors compare by [lem-sf-class-compact-support-comparison]. The individual proper direct-image site comparisons are the specified counit mates of [lem-weil-pbc-comparison-direct-image-canonical-mate], and compose by [prop-weil-pbc-comparison-direct-image]. Open extensions compare by [lem-cbc-proetale-extension-zero-comparison]. Derived scalar extension commutes with comparison pullback: on a K-flat representative both give ν^{-1}P⊗_A B; K-flat pullback and its tensor identification are [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback]. Applying [lem-weil-pbc-mate-pasting] to these inverse-image identities identifies the proper χ, the open β, and the exchanges E on the two sites. Thus the transpose calculation of steps 5–6 identifies their proper/open γ maps too. For refinement maps, [lem-sf-proper-open-comparison-site-normalization] explicitly identifies the named etale and pro-etale maps under these same comparisons. At the level of full compact supports the resulting composition comparison is the specified choice-independent α of [thm-sf-comp-composition]. Every factor of step 8 and every refinement map of step 7 is therefore its prescribed pro-etale factor, conjugated by the same site comparisons. Pulling back the etale equality and cancelling these comparisons gives the required pro-etale equality. All its arguments have bounded-below etale-origin witnesses by steps 1–2, so every invoked site comparison applies. This transports equality of B-linear arrows, not equality after forgetting their coefficients.
